precepts.text: Boaz answered Ruth that he would perform the kinsman's part, but there was a kinsman nearer than he.
precepts.point: The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

note.label: Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek

precepts.why:
Ruth's husband was dead, and Boaz was a near kinsman. “And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I. Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord liveth”.

Boaz answered Ruth that he would perform the kinsman's part, but there was a kinsman nearer than he. The part of a kinsman is the duty of the husband's brother in this law: take the wife of the dead and raise up his name. Boaz blessed her for seeking it, “inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich”, and all the city knew she was a virtuous woman.

precepts.text: Naomi had asked, Would ye tarry for sons till they were grown? Boaz's words point back to this: Ruth did what no young widow was expected to do, seeking the kinsman of her dead husband instead of following young men.
precepts.point: Boaz blessed her: thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich. Ruth could have gone after other men, but even as a Moabitess she was following the customs of Israel, trying to find someone to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth; she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

precepts.why:
Boaz's words point back to what Naomi had asked on the road out of Moab. “Turn again, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have an husband. If I should say, I have hope, if I should have an husband also to night, and should also bear sons; Would ye tarry for them till they were grown? would ye stay for them from having husbands?”

No young widow was expected to wait like that; Naomi released them because of it. Yet Ruth did what none expected: she followed not young men, whether poor or rich, but sought the kinsman of her dead husband. Even as a Moabitess she followed the customs of Israel, trying to raise up seed for her dead lord and keep his name in the earth. That is the kindness Boaz says she shewed more in the latter end than at the beginning: she was trying to do the right thing and keep the laws of Israel.

precepts.text: The virgins of Jabeshgilead had not known man by lying with any male; to know somebody in scripture means to lie with them.
precepts.point: Naomi answered, Sit still, my daughter, until thou know how the matter will fall: for the man will not be in rest until he have finished the thing this day.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

precepts.why:
Ruth lay at his feet until the morning, and rose up before one could know another. Knowing here is the same precept read in Judges 21. “And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh–gilead four hundred young virgins, that had known no man by lying with any male: and they brought them unto the camp to Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.”

The virgins had known no man by lying with any male; to know somebody in scripture means to lie with them, to have sex. So in this case, before one could know another means before they lay down together, and that is also why Boaz said, Let it not be known that a woman came into the floor.

precepts.text: The dictionary's own example of the skirt: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; the skirt is the extremity of the garment.
precepts.point: On the skirt: the Zondervan Compact Bible Dictionary (page 136) shows the basic garments in general use among men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and sandals. The word skirt in the KJV usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, with meanings of extremity and corner. Where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments, that is the bottom part of Saul's robe that David cut off privily.

note.label: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi

precepts.why:
Ruth said to Boaz, “spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.” That is the dictionary's own example of the skirt. The Zondervan Compact Bible Dictionary (page 136) shows the basic garments in general use among men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle and the cloak, with the headdress and sandals. The word skirt in the KJV usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, with meanings of extremity and corner. The skirt is the extremity of the garment.

Where we have our fringes attached to the borders of our garments, that is the bottom part of Saul's robe that David “cut off” “privily.”

And even for that, “David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt. And he said unto his men, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord’s anointed.” His men had said, “Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand.” Who is being referred to as the enemy? His own people: Saul was of the tribe of Benjamin, and David was of the tribe of Judah. “So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul.”

points: Naomi said, My daughter, shall I not seek rest for thee, that it may be well with thee? This is the same rest spoken of in chapter 1, rest in the house of a husband; and Boaz of their kindred was winnowing barley that night in the threshingfloor.

points: Her instructions: wash thyself, anoint thee, put thy raiment upon thee, get thee down to the floor, and make not thyself known unto the man until he has done eating and drinking; mark where he lies, uncover his feet, and lay thee down, and he will tell thee what thou shalt do. Ruth answered, All that thou sayest unto me I will do.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

points: Ruth did according to all her mother in law bade her. When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was merry, he lay down at the end of the heap of corn, and she came softly, uncovered his feet, and laid her down. At midnight the man was afraid, turned himself, and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

note.label: Ruth 3: The Skirt of the Near Kinsman

points: She answered, I am Ruth thine handmaid: spread therefore thy skirt over thine handmaid; for thou art a near kinsman.

On the skirt: Zondervan's Compact Bible Dictionary, page 137, explains that the basic garments of the men of biblical times were the inner tunic, the tunic coat, the girdle, and the cloak, with the headdress and the shoes or sandals; the word skirt in the Bible usually refers to an article of male, not female, clothing, and carries meanings such as extremity, as in Ruth 3:9. Asking Boaz to spread his skirt over her was asking the near kinsman to take her under his covering.
